title: Sell Mineral Rights in McMurray, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in McMurray, PA | Washington County
metaDescription: McMurray, PA (Peters Township) mineral owners: we buy Washington County Marcellus interests directly, even where suburban growth has complicated old farm titles.
heroLead: McMurray has grown into one of the more suburban corners of Washington County, but a surprising number of families here still hold mineral rights from the farmland this area used to be.
intro: Peters Township, where McMurray sits, has changed a lot over the past few decades, subdivisions and shopping centers now cover ground that was farmland when the original mineral severances happened. That growth doesn't erase the mineral rights underneath; it just means the surface owner and the mineral owner are often two completely different people or families now.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around McMurray directly. Whether you're the original family that held onto the minerals when the surface sold for development, or you inherited a small interest and aren't sure what it's connected to, we'll help you sort out what you actually have.

sections.heading: When Development Outpaces the Mineral Estate
paragraphs: It's common in growing parts of Washington County for oil and gas rights to have been severed from the surface decades before a farm ever became a subdivision. If your family sold surface land around McMurray years ago but kept the minerals, or if you inherited that severed interest, you may own rights under ground you'd never recognize as farmland today.

Operators have continued to develop the Marcellus in this part of Washington County even as the surface use has shifted, running laterals under residential areas from pads sited elsewhere, which is standard practice and doesn't require disturbing homes above.

sections.heading: Tracing a Severed Mineral Estate
paragraphs: We research Washington County Recorder of Deeds records to trace exactly when and how minerals were severed from the surface in your family's case, since that history determines what you own today regardless of what's built on top of the land now.
This kind of title work is more involved than a simple farm-to-farm inheritance, so we take the time to get it right and explain what we find.

sections.heading: What Your Interest Is Actually Worth
paragraphs: Value here depends on whether your severed interest sits within an active drilling unit, what the operator's division order shows for your decimal share, and recent royalty performance if the unit is producing. We'll walk through all of that with you before discussing a number.

faqs.question: My family sold the surface land decades ago near McMurray. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: Possibly. If your family's deed included a mineral reservation when the surface was sold, those rights may still belong to your family regardless of what's been built above them since. We'll research your specific title.

faqs.question: Is my interest less valuable because the land is now developed?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Mineral value depends on the formation below and whether your interest sits in an active unit, not on current surface use.

faqs.question: How do I know if my interest is in an active unit?
faqs.answer: We can check pooling and unit records for your parcel as part of our review, at no cost to you, before any offer is made.
